newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire talks on South African ship to start Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire talks on South African ship to start Sunday.

text.p: Shipborne talks between rebel leader Laurent Kabila and Zaire's ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko will begin on Sunday, South Africa's Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said late on Saturday.

Pahad, speaking after Kabila joined South Africa's Nelson Mandela on board the converted icebreaker SAS Outeniqua, said that the mediators had a commitment from Mobutu that he would join them on board on Sunday.
"Mr Kabila is here now and the meeting will start some time tomorrow and we hope they will begin to solve their problems," Pahad told reporters on board the South African naval ship.
Kabila, seen by reporters after his arrival by helicopter, appeared smiling and relaxed and wearing a dark-blue safari suit. He made no comment.

Mobutu and Mandela boarded the ship on Friday and sailed into international waters for a rendezvous Kabila failed to keep citing security concerns. Mobutu spent the night and Saturday in Congo's port of Pointe Noire, where the ship was moored.

Pahad said Kabila would spend the night on the ship and Mobutu would join the rebel leader and Mandela on Sunday morning. It was not immediately clear if the talks would be in international waters as initially planned.
